title: Krasnal-ID: fine-grained visual instance retrieval of Wrocław's dwarf statues
description:
A research prototype for fine-grained visual instance retrieval: identifying which of Wrocław's several hundred bronze dwarf statues (krasnale) a photograph shows. Every statue is the same semantic category, so the problem is instance recognition rather than classification — what separates them is a hat, a tool, a pose.

The central experiment asks how identification accuracy decays as the candidate pool grows, and whether narrowing that pool by location helps. It does not: proximity-based pools are consistently harder than random pools of the same size, because sculptors install related pieces near each other, so a small radius selects for a statue's own lookalikes.

Across a 306-statue pool with no fine-tuning, DINOv2 reaches 93.1% top-1 and CLIP 82.9%, under a leave-one-out protocol over 1,691 reference photographs. Also included: a candidate-pool-size ablation, a geographic ablation over derived coordinates, a trained-classifier comparison, confusion analysis, open-set rejection, and a lower bound on the query-domain gap between curated uploads and phone photographs.

This record archives the source code, documentation and published demo assets. The dataset itself — 1,691 attributed photographs, both backbones' embeddings and the evaluation folds — is published separately on Hugging Face and linked below.
